critical_findings: The signed tetrahedron coefficient q is retained with precisely the same eta^S factor; its nonnegativity is neither assumed nor required.
The Gram inequality is in the original probability inner product. The extra L(b,d) is nonnegative, so it can multiply an already established inequality; no weighted-PSD assertion is made.
The eta=0 case is separate; final powers have positive exponents. Arbitrary multiplicity, zero modes and eta=1 cause no division or lost term.
Component masses enter with exponent four minus six=-2; local normalization is explicit.
Independent-coordinate geometry is an additional hypothesis. Mixed cubic moments vanish there, not on arbitrary common-power hosts.
The full graph/entropy target is not a consequence of the returned finite coefficient proof. The proper shifted-prefix comparison remains unproved.
